a: Deliver assigned tasks well, ask good questions, learn the codebase.
Own features end-to-end, improve designs, mentor juniors lightly.
Lead ambiguous projects, raise quality bar, multiply team output.
Influence across teams, set technical direction, solve org-level problems.
Tech leads guide technical execution; managers own people and process.
Promotion packets show impact with metrics and stories, not only activity.
Higher levels handle larger scope, harder complexity, and more ambiguity.
Teaching others is a force multiplier recognized in leveling.
Make work visible with design docs, demos, and written outcomes.
Seek calibrated feedback from peers and managers regularly.
